append.text: **Ps 17:2 *Eu vos amarei, Senhor, minha força*:** held; in the same psalm *virtus* (17:33, 40) is *poder*, so the Latin's two words stay two. No reader remarked.

**Ps 17:3b *O meu Deus é o meu auxílio*: the Latinist asked for *auxiliador* again — minor on draft 1, MAJOR on draft 2 with the words unchanged; held (D24), recorded in Ps 17's decision `adjutor`.** Ps 17:2–3 sets four agent nouns side by side (*liberátor, adjútor, protéctor, suscéptor*): the Portuguese makes two agents (*libertador, protetor*) and two abstracts (*auxílio, amparo*). If Gustavo wants the series regular, Ps 17's decisions `adjutor` and `susceptor` turn both in one touch each.

**Ps 17:3c *e o meu amparo*: held against the Latinist — minor on draft 1 (*amparador*), MAJOR on draft 2 with the words unchanged and another fix (*aquele que me ampara*).** The pair noun/verb is heard across the psalm: 17:36a *déxtera tua suscépit me* → *a vossa direita me amparou* (one decision `susceptor`, two slots).

**Ps 17:3c *o chifre da minha salvação*:** kept; the blind reader heard a concrete horn and could not tell how it relates to salvation — not a mishearing, the image unexplained, as the Latin leaves it. The Latinist passed it twice.

**Ps 17:6 *As dores do inferno me cercaram*:** kept (DRB *the sorrows of hell*); the blind reader heard the torments of the damned first, as foreseen — here the parallel *laços da morte* in the same verse points to the realm of the dead. For Gustavo with the rest of the row.

**Ps 17 has *in conspéctu* four times in 17:2–25 (one decision `conspectu`):** *à vista de* where it is a predicate (17:23 *todos os seus juízos estão à minha vista*; 17:25 *à vista dos seus olhos*), *na sua presença* where it hangs beside a noun (17:7b *o meu clamor, na sua presença, entrou nos seus ouvidos*; 17:13 *Diante do clarão, na sua presença, passaram as nuvens*). In 17:13 the genitive *o clarão da sua presença* was refused by the Latinist (major): the phrase is adverbial, not the brightness's owner. Evidence that *à vista* serves predicates, *presença* the rest.

**Ps 17:15 *dissipávit eos* (people) → *e os dispersou*:** *dissipou* was unknown to the blind reader and heard as translated by the stylist. Cost: it meets *dispérgere* (88:11 *dispersísti inimícos tuos*; one Greek family, σκορπίζω / διασκορπίζω), never in one verse. Proposal: *dissipar* where the object is a thing (118:126 the law), *dispersar* where it is people.

**Ps 17:16a *fundaménta orbis terrárum* → *os fundamentos do mundo*:** *orbe* failed again — unknown to the blind reader (as in Ps 9) and 'livresca' for the stylist. **The Latin psalter never has *mundus* for the world** (grep: *mundus* is only 'clean', 18:13, 23:4, 50:4, 50:9, 50:12), so *mundo* collides with nothing. **Proposed: the row → *o mundo* in all 12 lines** (9:8b, 18:5, 23:1, 49:12, 71:8, 88:12, 92:1b, 95:10, 95:13, 97:6, 97:9 — *o orbe da terra* the option); Ps 9:8b would follow.

**Ps 17:16b *Ab increpatióne tua, Dómine* → *À vossa repreensão, Senhor*** (the noun; *À* = DRB's causal *At*). The same phrase opens 75:7, 103:7 and closes 79:17 (grep). No reader remarked; *ameaças* (MS1932) is the option.

**Ps 17:18 *quóniam confortáti sunt super me* → *porque se fortaleceram mais do que eu***: the verb held; *super me* said as the comparison it is (ὑπέρ), after the stylist heard *acima de mim* as a place.

**Ps 17:20 *Et edúxit me in latitúdinem* → *E me fez sair para a amplidão*** — the verse this row named; the stylist's best line of stage one; the blind reader heard a wide place and freedom. 17:37 *Dilatásti gressus meos* → *Alargastes* (same image, another word).
Ps 17:20 *quóniam vóluit me* → *porque me quis* (heard as 'loved me / chose me'); DRB's *was well pleased with me* is the option.

**Ps 17:23 *justítias ejus* (δικαιώματα) → *as suas justiças***, not *preceitos*: the stanza is built on the word (*justítiam meam* 17:21 — *justítias ejus* 23 — *justítiam meam* 25). The blind reader was unsure of the plural's sense (norms? acts of justice?); never heard as the courts. Option *os seus preceitos* (the Greek's, MS1932).

**Ps 17:24, 17:31 (*impollúta*), 17:33 → *imaculado* all three times**: one Greek word (ἄμωμος), so *impollútus* is merged by D15's test (*impoluto* the option). The blind reader listed *imaculado* as unknown (twice) — surprising; kept.

Ps 17:23 *justítias ejus non répuli a me* → *e não afastei de mim as suas justiças*. So in 17:22 *nec ímpie gessi a Deo meo* took *apartar-se* (*e não me apartei impiamente do meu Deus* — the Latinist's major, taken) to keep the two verbs apart.

**Ps 17:19 transitive and hostile: *Prævenérunt me in die afflictiónis meæ* → *Surpreenderam-me***, one verb with 17:6 *præoccupavérunt me láquei mortis* → *me surpreenderam* — one Greek verb (προέφθασάν με) in both, D15's test. The Latinist (minor) wanted *Anteciparam-se a mim*; refused. The friendly transitive places (20:4, 58:10, 87:14) are not settled by this.
**Ps 17:29 *Porque vós iluminais a minha lâmpada, Senhor: * meu Deus, iluminai as minhas trevas*** — the stylist's best line of stage two; no reader remarked on *lâmpada*.
Ps 17:29 *illúminas … illúmina* → *iluminais … iluminai* (safe: past *iluminei*); the Latin's repetition kept; the stylist's best line.
**Ps 17:31 *elóquia Dómini igne examináta* → *as palavras do Senhor, examinadas no fogo*** (D27), verbless as the Latin; the blind reader heard 'put to the test and proved true'. Passed the Latinist.
**Ps 17:31, as D27 ruled: *as palavras do Senhor, examinadas no fogo*** — held; the Latinist passed it; the blind reader heard it rightly.

**Ps 17:33, 17:40 *præcínxit me virtúte … præcinxísti me virtúte ad bellum* → *me cingiu de poder … me cingistes de poder para a guerra*** — the row's word, kept apart from 17:2 *fortitúdo* → *força* in the same psalm (DRB and MS1932 have *strength / força* here, which would merge them). Passed the Latinist twice; no other reader remarked.

**Ps 17:34, the place this row was tried on: *Que aperfeiçoou os meus pés como os das corças*** — held against the stylist, who found the vowels of *aperfeiçoou os* hard to say daily (*tornou perfeitos* is the option). Passed the Latinist twice.
Ps 17:34 *et super excélsa státuens me* → *e sobre as alturas me firmando* — the row's verb, the participle kept as a gerund at the Latinist's request.
Ps 17:36a *e a vossa direita me amparou*; the blind reader heard the right hand first.

Ps 17:36b twice (*E a vossa disciplina me corrigiu até o fim, * e a vossa própria disciplina me ensinará*); the blind reader heard correction/punishment first, instruction second — both are in the verse.

append.row: | in finem | para sempre where it says perpetuity (each psalm decides) | working (D27) | Ps 9:7a
append.text: **Ps 17:36b, the place D27 named: *corréxit me in finem* → *me corrigiu até o fim*** — not *para sempre*: nothing is negated (the failure at 9:19 was *não … até o fim*), and with a past act *para sempre* would make the correcting perpetual; εἰς τέλος, DRB *unto the end*, MS1932 *até ao fim*. The blind reader heard 'corrected me completely' first — the other sense of εἰς τέλος — and 'until the end of my life' second. Passed the Latinist twice. So *in finem* has two renderings, as D27 allowed: *para sempre* (perpetuity) and *até o fim* (Ps 17 decision `finem`, *para sempre* the option).
Ps 17:38 *Pérsequar inimícos meos et comprehéndam illos* → *Perseguirei os meus inimigos e os prenderei* — the row applied at one of its two *pérsequi* places; passed all readers.

**Ps 17:38 *donec defíciant* (enemies pursued) → *até que desfaleçam*:** with persons, but meaning 'give out', not 'be gone' (11:2) — the blind reader heard 'until they lose their strength' (and listed the word as unknown). Holds there.
Ps 17:39 *Confríngam illos* (ἐκθλίψω) → *Eu os quebrarei*; no reader remarked (the blind reader heard physical violence).
Ps 17:39 *nec póterunt stare* → *e não poderão estar de pé*; no reader remarked.
Ps 17:40, 17:49 (both in this row's list): *os que contra mim se levantavam* (the stylist's order), *acima dos que se levantam contra mim*; passed all readers.
Ps 17:41 *et odiéntes me disperdidísti* → *e exterminastes os que me odeiam*.

**Ps 17:46 *Fílii aliéni … fílii aliéni* → *Os filhos estranhos … os filhos estranhos*:** the blind reader heard 'other people's children' or 'odd children' first and did not perceive foreigners — inside the row's 'not one's own'; kept, *filhos alheios* and *filhos de estrangeiros* are options.
Ps 17:46 *fílii aliéni inveteráti sunt* → *os filhos estranhos envelheceram*; heard literally (grew old) first.
Ps 17:46 *a sémitis suis* → *fora das suas veredas*: *veredas* listed as unknown by the blind reader once more; kept (D15).
Ps 17:47 *et exaltétur Deus salútis meæ* → *e exalte-se o Deus da minha salvação* (9:33's jussive); 17:49 *exaltábis me* → *me exaltareis*.
Ps 17:50 *Proptérea confitébor tibi in natiónibus, Dómine* → *Por isso vos darei graças entre as nações, Senhor* — D5 held; no reader remarked.

**Ps 17:50 *nómini tuo psalmum dicam* → *e entoarei um salmo ao vosso nome*:** *psalmum dícere* renders ψαλῶ, the verb *psállere* renders elsewhere, so D25's verb serves with the Latin's singular noun (D15's test); echoes 7:18b. Passed the Latinist twice; *direi um salmo* is the option.
Ps 17:51 *Magníficans salútes Regis ejus* → *Engrandecendo as salvações do seu Rei* (the plural kept; the participle as a gerund, dangling as the Latin's does).

**Ps 17:51 *Christo suo David* → *o seu Cristo, Davi*:** the blind reader heard Jesus, and could not tell whether Christ and David are one person or two — the Latin's apposition allows the Church's reading; held (D19).
Ps 17:48 *et subdis pópulos sub me* → *e sujeitais os povos sob mim*: *subdere* takes *subjícere*'s verb (one Greek verb, ὑποτάσσω); 143:2 *qui subdit pópulum meum sub me* should follow.

Ps 17:18, 30, 44, 49 — four times, each with a source named (*de inimícis*, *a tentatióne*, *de contradictiónibus*, *a viro iníquo*) → *arrancar* throughout; no reader remarked, and *serei arrancado da tentação* (17:30) was heard rightly.
Ps 17:36a *protectiónem salútis tuæ* → *a proteção da vossa salvação* (the Latin's *tuæ*, not the Greek's μου).

Ps 17:35 *Qui docet manus meas ad prǽlium* → *Que ensina as minhas mãos para a batalha*, echoed by 17:36b *docébit* → *me ensinará*; the stylist asked for *instrui* (refused: the echo, and *instruir* is *erudíre*'s).

terms: | protéctor | protetor (*O meu protetor*; *o Senhor se fez o meu protetor*) | open | Ps 17:3c, 17:19, 17:31 (one decision `protector`, three slots); 19 lines in the psalter (grep), often beside *adjútor* (27:7, 32:20, 39:18, 113:17–19 *adjútor eórum et protéctor eórum est*) and *refúgium*. ὑπερασπιστής, the one who holds a shield over. The cognate, an agent noun as the Latin's; stays apart from *suscéptor → amparo* (D19) and *adjútor → auxílio*. The Latinist passed it four times; no reader remarked. Options *defensor* (MS1932's word for *suscéptor* — they would cross), *escudo* (DM1962, the Hebrew's image; refused). **Ps 17:2–3 sets the four titles side by side** — see the rows *adjútor* and *suscéptor* for the mixed series it makes |

| firmaméntum (God as support) | esteio (*o Senhor é o meu esteio*) | open | Ps 17:2 (also 24:14 *Firmaméntum est Dóminus timéntibus eum*, 70:3 *Quóniam firmaméntum meum, et refúgium meum es tu*). στερέωμα, 'a support, a prop' (L&S). **The blind reader heard *o meu firmamento* FIRST as 'my sky'** — Portuguese *firmamento* is only the vault. The Latin keeps one word for the vault (18:2, 150:1 *in firmaménto virtútis ejus*) and the stay; Portuguese cannot, so: *firmamento* where it is the sky, *esteio* where God holds up (24:14, 70:3); 71:16, 72:4 *firmaméntum in plaga eórum*, 104:16 *omne firmaméntum panis* decide locally (all nine lines by grep). Options in Ps 17: *o meu firmamento*, *o meu firme apoio* (MS1932), *a minha firmeza*. The Latinist passed *esteio*; the stylist did not remark |
| liberátor | libertador | working | Ps 17:2, 17:48 (*meu libertador dos meus inimigos irados*); 69:6, 143:2 (grep) |

| præoccupáre | surpreender (*os laços da morte me surpreenderam*) | open | Ps 17:6 only (grep); one Greek verb with 17:19 *prævenérunt* (προέφθασαν), which shares it. L&S 'seize upon beforehand … take, catch'. MS1932's verb |

| calígo | névoa escura (*e havia uma névoa escura sob os seus pés*) | open | Ps 17:10 (γνόφος); 96:2 *Nubes et calígo in circúitu ejus* will meet it beside *nubes → nuvem*. *trevas* is *ténebræ*'s (17:12); *caligem* needs a footnote. *havia* supplied at the stylist's request |
| latíbulum | esconderijo (*E fez das trevas o seu esconderijo*) | working | Ps 17:12 only (grep); ἀποκρυφή; *refúgio* is *refúgium*'s |

| carbónes (ignis) | carvões (de fogo) | working | Ps 17:9 *carvões foram acesos por ele*, 17:13 = 17:14 *granizo e carvões de fogo*; 119:4 *carbónibus desolatóriis*, 139:11 *cadent super eos carbónes* (grep). MS1932's word; *brasas* (DM1962) is the option — *brasas foram acesas* says the fire twice |

| vocem dare (dedit vocem suam) | fazer ouvir a voz (*e o Altíssimo fez ouvir a sua voz*) | open | Ps 17:14; **45:7 *dedit vocem suam, mota est terra*** and 67:34b *dabit voci suæ vocem virtútis* will meet it (grep). The idiom, as MS1932 and DM1962; *deu a sua voz* is not said. No reader remarked |
| fumus / grando | fumaça / granizo | working | Ps 17:9, 17:13–14; *fumo* is tobacco in Brazil, *saraiva* European; 148:8 *grando*, 101:4 *sicut fumus* |

| pónere + predicate (made X Y) | the verb the Portuguese build wants: *fazer de* (17:12 *fez das trevas o seu esconderijo*), *tornar* + adjective (17:33 *tornou imaculado o meu caminho*), *fazer … como* (17:35 *fizestes os meus braços como um arco de bronze*) | open | Ps 17 (decision `posuit`, three slots). Draft 4 had *fazer* all three times; the stylist heard *fez imaculado* as a calque. *pôr* (the Latin's verb) is the option; *láqueum pónere → pôr um laço* stands |

| assúmere (me) | recolher (*e me recolheu de muitas águas*) | open | Ps 17:17, beside *accépit me → me tomou* (ἔλαβεν … προσελάβετο). The other two places (grep): 26:10 *Dóminus autem assúmpsit me* (*o Senhor me recolheu* — fits), 64:5 *quem elegísti, et assumpsísti*. Options *tomar consigo*, MS1932 *tirar* |

| edúcere | fazer sair (*E me fez sair para a amplidão*) | open | Ps 17:20 — the stylist's best line of stage one. *conduzir* fails rule 3 at the imperative (*conduzi-me*, D22). Twelve other lines (grep), most with *de* (30:5, 39:3, 77:16, 106:14 *edúxit eos de ténebris*, 106:28, 142:11b; 141:8 *Educ de custódia* is an imperative) — those may want *tirar de* |

| ímpie gérere a | apartar-se impiamente de (*e não me apartei impiamente do meu Deus*) | open | Ps 17:22 only (grep). The calque ἠσέβησα ἀπό; **the Latinist marked DRB/MS1932's *contra o meu Deus* MAJOR** (the separation lost). *apartar* rather than his *afastar*, so that 17:23 *répuli a me → afastei* keeps its own verb. *apartar-se* is also *declináre a*'s (open row), which Ps 17 does not have |

| observáre se ab | guardar-se de (*e me guardarei da minha iniquidade*) | open | Ps 17:24, two verses after *custodívi → guardei*: one Greek verb (φυλάσσω) in both, D15's test; MS1932. *serváre (a law) → observar* stands |

| pervérti (passive, of God) | perverter-se (*e com o perverso vos pervertereis*) | open | Ps 17:27 only; the Latin's jolt kept (DRB *thou wilt be perverted*; the Greek is active, διαστρέψεις). **The blind reader heard 'God will become perverse' first — which is what the Latin says**; the Latinist passed it twice. Options *sereis perverso* (the other three members' build), *sereis pervertido* (a sexual word in Brazil), MS1932's gloss *sereis como ele merece* (refused, D2). For Gustavo's ear |

| transgrédi (murum) | transpor (*e no meu Deus transporei o muro*) | open | Ps 17:30 only; ὑπερβήσομαι. Listed as unknown by the blind reader, who still paraphrased 'I will get over an obstacle'. Options *passarei por cima do muro*, MS1932 *trespassarei* (to pierce) |

| supplantáre | derrubar (*e derrubastes sob mim os que contra mim se levantavam*) | open | Ps 17:40; L&S 'trip up one's heels, throw down'. 16:13 *supplánta eum*, 36:31 *non supplantabúntur gressus ejus*, 139:5 *supplantáre gressus meos* (grep) — with *gressus* as object *fazer tropeçar* is the natural verb and is the option; the cognate *suplantar* means surpass |

| dare dorsum (inimícos … dorsum) | dar as costas de (*E me destes as costas dos meus inimigos*) | open | Ps 17:41 (the stylist's wording after *de costas* was his worst line and puzzled the blind reader); the double accusative as a genitive. 20:13 *pones eos dorsum* will want the same image (grep: dorsum also 68:24, 80:7, 128:3, the literal back) |

| commínuere / delére | esmigalhar / apagar (*E eu os esmigalharei como o pó … como a lama das ruas os apagarei*) | open | Ps 17:43; *delére* → *apagar* is the verb 50:3b *dele iniquitátem meam* and 50:11 will want; 68:29 *deleántur de libro vivéntium*, 108:13–14. No reader remarked |

| contradíctio | contenda (*das contendas do povo*) | open | Ps 17:44 (ἀντιλογία). **The blind reader heard *as contradições do povo* first as the people's inconsistencies.** 30:21 *a contradictióne linguárum*, 54:10; 80:8, 105:32 *aqua contradictiónis* is a proper name (Meribah) and may keep *contradição*. No *contentio* in the psalter (grep) |

| claudicáre | mancar (*e mancaram fora das suas veredas*) | working | Ps 17:46 only (grep); *coxearam* was unknown to the blind reader and uncurrent to the stylist; *claudicar* (MS1932) is literary |

| cervus | cervo; **17:34 *corças*** | open | **Ps 17:34 *os meus pés como os dos cervos* was heard by the blind reader as *servos*** (homophones in Brazil). There → *como os das corças* (the female; no homophone; gender lost). 28:9, 41:2 *cervus ad fontes aquárum*, 103:17 have the animal's context and may keep *cervo*. *veado* (MS1932) is also a slur in Brazil |

| subtus / sub (me, pedes) | sob (*sob mim*, *sob os meus pés*) | working | Ps 17:10, 37, 39, 40, 48 — one preposition for the Latin's run of *subtus* (the stylist asked for *sob mim* at 17:40 and 17:48). 8:8 has *debaixo dos seus pés* (*subjecísti sub pédibus ejus*): a psalm that wants the living preposition may keep it |

| semen (offspring) | descendência (*e com a sua descendência para sempre*) | open | Ps 17:51; 16 other lines (grep: 20:11, 21:24, 21:25, 21:31, 24:13, 36:25, 36:26, 36:28, 68:37, 88:4, 88:30, 88:36, 101:29, 104:6, 105:27, 111:2) — *semen Ábraham* (104:6) and *semen Jacob* (21:24) will test it. *semente* (DRB *seed*) keeps the image and is the option — for Gustavo's ear; MS1932 *posteridade* |

| in audítu auris | ao ouvir com o ouvido (*ao ouvir com o ouvido, obedeceu-me*) | open | Ps 17:45; the pleonasm kept (εἰς ἀκοὴν ὠτίου). Options *mal me ouviu*, MS1932 *ao ouvir a minha voz* (a voice supplied) |

| vestígia | pegadas (*e não se enfraqueceram as minhas pegadas*) | open | Ps 17:37 (ἴχνη); DRB and MS1932 *feet*. The blind reader noted that *pegadas* are usually marks on the ground, and heard the sense (steps firm). 16:5 *ut non moveántur vestígia mea* is the only other *vestígia mea* (grep) |
| vindíctæ | vinganças (*Deus, que me dais vinganças*) | working | Ps 17:48 (plural kept); 93:1 *Deus ultiónum* is another word |
formulas: | *grando et carbónes ignis* (17:13 = 17:14, the colon repeated) | *granizo e carvões de fogo* | working — Ps 17 |

| *Et retríbuet mihi Dóminus secúndum justítiam meam* (17:21a = 17:25a) | *E o Senhor me retribuirá segundo a minha justiça* | working — Ps 17 (decision `retribuet`: one verb three times; MS1932 varies it) |
| *Ab increpatióne tua* (17:16b; 75:7, 103:7; 79:17 *ab increpatióne vultus tui*) | *À vossa repreensão* | open — Ps 17 |
| *præcínxit / præcinxísti me virtúte* (17:33, 17:40; cf. 92:1a *indútus est Dóminus fortitúdinem, et præcínxit se*) | *me cingiu / me cingistes de poder* | open (hangs on *virtus*) — Ps 17 |
| *Vivit Dóminus* (17:47) | *Vive o Senhor* | working — Ps 17; the blind reader heard 'the Lord is alive' first, an acclamation second |
| *qui subdit / subdis pópulos sub me* (17:48; 143:2 *qui subdit pópulum meum sub me*) | *que sujeitais os povos sob mim* | open — Ps 17; **Ps 143:2 should copy it** |
